{{Top}}
{{Youmay|the part|the [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] as a whole}}
[[File:Lightsabers-NEGWT.png|thumb|right|250px|Examples of standard, [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed]], and [[Curved-hilt lightsaber/Legends|curved hilts]].]]
{{Quote|Touch the brightly-colored button up there by the pommel&hellip;.|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]|<ref name="Star Wars (1977) 2">[[Star Wars (1977) 2|''Star Wars'' (1977) 2]]</ref>}}
'''Lightsaber hilts''' were the basic, all-encompassing part of a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]. A combination handgrip, [[Blade emitter/Legends|blade emitter]], [[Activation stud|activator switch]] and [[Diatium power cell/Legends|power source]], it held within the inner workings of the weapon that allowed it to produce its distinctive energy-based blade. The first hilts were produced as early as the advent of the lightsaber itself, approximately [[15,500 BBY]]; though cumbersome and requiring a backpack-mounted power source, the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] nonetheless began to embrace the technology. Eventually these hilts evolved to only require a small belt-mounted pack, and again to a fully self-contained weapon system; such designs saw service as early as [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]] at the start of the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]]. Over the thousands of years that followed, power technology and indeed the construction of lightsaber hilts continued to evolve, eventually encompassing [[Shoto lightsaber/Legends|shotos]], shorter hilts used in the off-hand, as well as [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed]], [[Curved-hilt lightsaber/Legends|curved-hilt]], and [[Dual-phase lightsaber/Legends|dual-phase]] designs. There are many unique hilts, such as the lightsaber hilt of [[Gungi/Legends|Gungi]], a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Initiate]]. His hilt was made from the wood of a [[Brylark tree/Legends|Brylark tree]], which is as strong as metal.

Both the Jedi and the [[Sith Order]] used lightsaber hilts; the former regarding them as tools rather than weapons, while the latter sought to use their sabers to fuel their quest for power. Both Orders saw the construction of a lightsaber hilt to be one of the primary stages of a being's development within their ranks, mostly signifying that a [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] or [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] was ready to ascend to the next level. Though double-bladed hilts were typically associated with the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], practitioners of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]], those who followed the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]] occasionally preferred these over the commonly-accepted use of single hilts in [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|battle]]. Despite [[First Jedi Purge|two]] [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|attempts]] to eradicate the Jedi, the technology of lightsaber hilts continued to live on as the Order that had originally supported them rose anew. In addition, other Force-using traditions, such as the [[Jensaarai/Legends|Jensaarai]], constructed lightsaber hilts.

==Technology and construction==
===Components===
[[File:LightsaberConstruction-SWE.png|thumb|left|280px|The disassembled inner components of a lightsaber hilt.]]
A lightsaber hilt contained many components, all of which were hand-selected by the Force-user who constructed it and tuned to be in harmony with each other at the completion of the weapon's creation. From [[Focusing lens/Legends|focusing lens]] to [[Pommel cap/Legends|pommel cap]],<ref name="ijedi">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref> such components typically included a [[Blade emitter/Legends|blade emitter shroud]], magnetic stabilizing loop followed by a ring tuning flange<ref name="cvd">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> to ensure that the activated blade did not in turn burn through the hilt.<ref name="ijedi" /> Immediately below and mounted internally lay the blade arc tip, followed on the outside by the [[Blade power adjustment knob|blade power adjustment]] and blade length adjustment knobs. Following the arc tip were mounted the blade energy channel which was nested amongst the cycling field energizers. Within the crystal energy chamber below this lay the focusing [[Lightsaber crystal/Legends|crystals]], the focusing crystal activator and the primary crystal which was attached to the primary crystal mount and situated between the lightsaber energy gate.<ref name="cvd" />

The primary crystal mount was in turn connected to the [[Diatium power cell/Legends|diatium power cell]], which served as the primary power source of the weapon.<ref name="ijedi" /> The power cell was in turn wrapped beneath the power field conductor, power vortex ring and an [[Inert power insulator/Legends|inert power insulator]]. Rounding out the components that went into a typical hilt were the handgrip connector and a sturdy belt ring.<ref name="cvd" />

Gathering the various components to construct a lightsaber was relatively simple, given the utilitarian nature of the materials involved; typically, these were readily available commercially, with the exception of the crystals.<ref name="ijedi" /> In the pre-[[Ruusan campaign|Ruusan]] Jedi Order, such crystals could be found within Force-sensitive locations from across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]; these were typically places that resonated with a powerful dark or light-side presence in the Force. In the wake of the [[New Sith Wars]], however, the Jedi chose to limit their crystal harvesting to the frigid world of [[Ilum/Legends|Ilum]], which brimmed with [[Adegan crystal/Legends|Adegan crystals]] that only produced blue and green blades. In the [[New Jedi Order]] this restriction was not carried through, and Jedi of that era once again used a wide variety of gemstones that produced different-colored blades.<ref name="egttf">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>

===Assembly===
[[File:Marek_saber_construction.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[Galen Marek]] telekinetically assembles his lightsaber.]]
Nearly every lightsaber hilt was unique in its construction, born of the Force-user who created it and using whatever materials were at hand; typically, such weapons were created over a span of months.<ref name="ijedi" /> Ideally, the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] or [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] who created it would go into deep [[Meditation/Legends|Meditation]], poring over each individual component to be added and thus forging a connection with it through [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].

While the individual components of a lightsaber were relatively common and could be mass-produced, aligning them and the crystals required a supernaturally-steady hand guided by the Force. No attempt to mass-produce lightsabers ever succeeded.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

==Types of hilts==
Though each hilt was unique to the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-user]] who created it, a [[Lightsaber/Legends#Hilt_variations|number of basic designs]] evolved [[Timeline of galactic history/Legends|over the millennia]]. Included among these were the [[Shoto lightsaber/Legends|shoto]], a shorter design that was balanced to allow a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] or [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] to use it comfortably in the off-hand;<ref name="marvel96">[[Star Wars (1977) 96|''Star Wars'' (1977) 96]]</ref> the [[Curved-hilt lightsaber/Legends|curved-hilt lightsaber]], which was developed to accommodate the needs of [[Form II/Legends|Form II: Makashi]];<ref name="epII">{{Film|II}}</ref> the [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed lightsaber]], also known as the saberstaff, which projected a beam from each end of the hilt;<ref name="ep1">{{Film|I}}</ref> and, least common of all, the [[Dual-phase lightsaber/Legends|dual-phase lightsaber]]. Dual-phase hilts were unique in that they allowed the person who had created them to adjust the beam length of their weapon; one setting typically used a standard blade length of approximately a meter or more, while the other setting could extend the blade out to three full meters. Such weapons were rare because there was no known style or practical use for the extended beam, beyond a startling surprise for an opponent.<ref name="ijedi" />

===Shotos and short lightsabers===
{{Main|Lightsaber shoto}}

Shotos, or short lightsabers as they were known during the [[Old Sith Wars]], were secondary weapons that served much the same purpose as a dagger in the off-hand of a combatant. They typically utilized the same components of regular lightsaber hilts, however both the hilt itself and the blade it produced were significantly shorter. Some Jedi or Sith, rather than using a normal-style lightsaber and a shoto, would instead use two shotos, one in each hand.<ref name="kotor">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> Another style of short lightsaber, called a [[Guard shoto/Legends|guard shoto]], utilized a rare perpendicular grip on the hilt. Many years later, shotos would see a resurgence as another form of energy-based weapon similar to the lightsaber, the [[Lightwhip/Legends|lightwhip]], came to be developed. Luke Skywalker constructed and utilized his own shoto after confronting the whip utilized by [[Lumiya]] for the first time, using it to great effect the next time the pair met in combat.<ref name="marvel96" />

[[File:Lightsabers_galore_JATM.jpg|thumb|250px|An assortment of lightsabers hilts, including: [[Curved-hilt lightsaber/Legends|curved-hilt]], [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed]], [[Guard shoto/Legends|guard shoto]], [[Interlocking hilt|fiber-cord linked]], and others.]]

==Behind the scenes==
Lightsaber hilts appear, either directly or indirectly, in every work within the ''Star Wars'' library that also features lightsabers themselves. Their first reference was in the novelization of [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope]], when [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] presents [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] with [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|his father's]] lightsaber in the farmer's hut on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Since then they have persisted as one of the most iconic symbols of the ''Star Wars'' saga, including the films themselves and the litany of [[canon]]ical and non-canonical works. In early drafts of the script for ''A New Hope'', however, these weapons were intended to be commonplace, in that common [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] and [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] troopers alike used them.<ref name="Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays">''[[Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays]]''</ref>

Though most works that reference lightsaber construction use a more complicated method, within ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'', much like [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic|its predecessor]], the process is markedly simplified. For instance, lightsaber construction is confined to a few simple parts and takes only "a few hours" to accomplish.<ref name="kotor2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref> However, most other [[canon]]ical sources state that construction can take up to a few months, with many more parts needed besides.<ref name="ijedi" />

Lightsaber hilts can be seen in the real world through a number of different series of ''Star Wars''-licensed toys. Ranging from cheap plastic hilts that "grow" a segmented, fitted blade when a button is pressed and the hilt is "drawn", to hilts with blades lit from within by [[Wikipedia:flashlight|flashlights]] that also emit sounds and other features, to high-quality metal hilts that mount a blade with in-built [[Wikipedia:LED|LED]] lights. These hilts, manufactured and marketed by companies such as [[Wikipedia:Master Replicas|Master Replicas]], are sometimes used in fan-organized sparring matches, such as those seen at various ''Star Wars'' conventions. In addition, more mechanically-inclined fans produce their own hilts through the use of a metalworking [[Wikipedia:lathe|lathe]] and inner wiring to produce lights, etc. for use in costumes. These hilts are sometimes fitted with custom "blades" that also emit a colored light and can be used in mock lightsaber duels.
